title: Why Ukraine Keeps Hitting the Crimean Bridge

scenes.text: Ukraine just dropped part of Russia's nineteen-kilometre bridge to Crimea... and it keeps hitting it.
It crosses the Kerch Strait, linking Russia directly to occupied Crimea.
Russia seized Crimea in 2014, then built road and rail crossings to hold it.
Trains and trucks carry fuel, freight and military supplies onto the peninsula.
In November 2026, Ukrainian strikes brought down the main road arch.
The railway was damaged too, and trains were repeatedly halted.
Russia still has a land route through occupied southern Ukraine.
But pushing traffic onto that route makes supplying Crimea slower and riskier.
And every hit damages a symbol Putin himself opened in 2018.
Can Russia keep Crimea supplied without it? Tell me below.
